# Spring Boot host config. H2 in-memory in the same JVM; Flyway migrates the schema up on boot from
# db/migration; Actuator health is the readiness probe.

# In-memory H2 (dies with the JVM = clean per-run reset).
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:officehq;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=
# Pooled connections are never retired: when HikariCP closes one at its default 30 min
# max-lifetime, this in-memory H2 closes under the remaining sessions and every later statement
# fails with "The database has been closed" while the health probe stays UP. 0 means no lifetime.
spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=0

# Flyway owns the schema. JPA does not create tables.
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
# Close the persistence context at the end of the request, not during view rendering.
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# Readiness probe.
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true

# The SPA is served from src/main/resources/static (built there by bin/build); deep-link
# fallback is in SpaConfig.java.

# Audit sink: one record per line to this known file, so tests assert side-effects by reading it.
# bin/start passes an absolute path via AUDIT_FILE; default is .run/audit.log.
app.audit.file=${AUDIT_FILE:.run/audit.log}

Each claim now shows its status log, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

I ran the tests on port 3417 with `PORT=3417 bin/e2e`, because something else was already using port 3000. I didn't stop that process since I don't know what it is.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new table, `V29__claim_log.sql`, holds one line per status a claim has had: the status, who made the change, the sheet's today at the time, and the due at that moment.
- **Server:** a log line is written every time a claim's status is set:
  - adding a claim writes its DRAFT line;
  - open, settle, void and a settle that becomes PENDING each write a line;
  - approve writes a SETTLED line;
  - reject writes an OPEN line.
  
  The due recorded is what the claim shows right after the change, so a settled claim's line includes any late charge it had built up. Claims sent to the screen now carry their log, oldest first.
- **Front end:** each claim row has a new "Log" column listing lines like `OPEN by uma on 2026-03-30 due=10.00`, each marked `claim-log-line`. A claim with no due shows `due=n/a`.

**Two things to know:**
- Claims that existed before this change have an empty log, because their past status changes were never recorded. That only matters for data that already exists, not for new sheets.
- The log is loaded alongside each claim with its own database query per claim. That's fine at the current size, but it could become slow on a sheet with a very large number of claims.
